title: Pahlavi Texts, Part I: Bundahis, Bahman Yast and Shayast la-Shayast
transliteration: Bundahišn, Bahman Yašt, Šāyist nē Šāyist
dateDisplay: 9th century CE, from older oral and written sources
attributionNote: These Pahlavi books are anonymous compilations of the Zoroastrian priesthood, written down in the ninth century from earlier Middle Persian tradition. They are not Avestan scripture and are not ascribed to Zarathushtra.
description: The first volume of West's Pahlavi Texts contains the Bundahis, the Zoroastrian account of creation: the primal conflict of Ohrmazd and Ahriman, the making of the sky, water, earth, plants, animals and humanity, and the final renovation. With it are the Selections of Zad-sparam, the apocalyptic Bahman Yast, and the Shayast la-Shayast, the Pahlavi manual of religious law and penance.
historicalContext: The Bundahis and its companion texts survive only in ninth-century Pahlavi compilations, though they preserve much older Mazdean teaching. E. W. West translated them for the Sacred Books of the East, volume 5 (1880), the first volume of his five-volume Pahlavi series.
availabilityNote: Complete for this volume. The Bundahis (34 chapters), the Selections of Zad-sparam, the Bahman Yast and the Shayast la-Shayast are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one chapter per page. The volume's introduction and editorial observations are not part of the work.
